title: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
summary: On 3 October 1935, Fascist Italy invaded the Ethiopian Empire without a declaration of war, crossing the Mareb River and launching aerial bombardments. Employing overwhelming mechanized force and prohibited chemical weapons—chiefly aerial spraying of sulfur mustard gas—Italian forces broke Ethiopian resistance and entered Addis Ababa in May 1936. The conflict demonstrated the failure of League of Nations collective security, exposed the inability of international treaties to restrain fascist aggression, and galvanized anti-colonial movements across Africa and the global diaspora.

where.historical_name: Ethiopian Empire (invaded by Kingdom of Italy)

importance.justification: The invasion fatally undermined the League of Nations' system of collective security, saw the large-scale military use of prohibited chemical weapons, and presaged the Axis aggression of World War II.

audience_note: Documents unprovoked colonial invasion, aerial bombardment of civilians, and widespread deployment of prohibited mustard gas.
